title: SnapOtter
name: snapotter
description: File toolkit with over 200 tools for images, PDFs, video, audio and data files, like compressing, converting, OCR, background removal and transcription, with saved pipelines and a REST API. Source: https://github.com/snapotter-hq/SnapOtter

env.name: SNAPOTTER_DB_PASSWORD
env.label: Database password (required)
env.description: For the bundled Postgres. It goes into a connection URL, so stick to letters and digits. Generate one with: openssl rand -hex 16. Keep it the same when you redeploy.

env.name: SNAPOTTER_PORT
env.label: Host port for the web UI

note: Fill in the database password before you deploy, since the stack won't start without it (openssl rand -hex 16), and keep it the same on every redeploy. It's a big pull, about 3.7 GB on amd64 (the CUDA libraries for NVIDIA cards ride along) and 1.8 GB on arm64. Open it on port 1349 and log in with admin / admin, which makes you pick a new password straight away, so do that before anyone else on your network does. Add more people under Settings --> People. Out of the box it sends anonymous usage stats and crash reports to its makers, so switch that off under Settings --> System Settings --> Privacy if you'd rather it didn't. Results you don't save to Files are deleted after 72 hours. The AI tools (background removal, upscaling and so on) need their models installed first under Settings --> AI Features, at several GB each. Saved files and those models live in the snapotter-data volume, and accounts, settings and pipelines in Postgres (postgres-data). Docs: docs.snapotter.com
